meeting_header: Date: 2026-12-18 | Time: 15:00–15:52 UTC | Duration: 52 minutes | Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ravi Kapoor (Redwood SE), Dr. Lena Ortiz (Atlas Legal), Marcus Lee (Atlas Platform), Priya Singh (Atlas Procurement), Evan Zhao (Atlas Security)
summary: Redwood and Atlas Biotech reviewed the MSA/DPA redlines, SLA targets, pricing bands (committed vs burst), and onboarding pilot plan. Legal open items were indemnity, data residency and audit rights. Engineering requested a 2-hour pilot with sample traffic and clarified VPC/KMS options for private deployment. Next steps: Redwood to send redlined MSA/DPA and pilot runbook; Atlas to provide traffic profile and legal comments.
transcript:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you making time on a Friday, we'll run about 45 to 55 minutes, lots to cover — MSA/DPA, SLAs, pilot.
[00:12] Dr. Lena Ortiz: Thanks Maya, yes we have a few legal points up front.
[00:18] Marcus: Hi, Marcus here — I can jump into the technical asks later.
[00:22] Priya: And Priya from procurement. Quick note we need final pricing approval to pull purchase order.
[00:30] Maya: Great, so agenda — quick intro, go through the MSA redlines, DPA questions, SLA thresholds, pricing bands, then pilot details and next steps. Ravi, you good to open on the technical bits?
[00:40] Ravi: Yeah thanks, hi all, I'll try to be concise — our pilot offers both hosted and private options; for Atlas we recommended private VPC with customer-managed KMS given you mentioned regulated data.
[00:50] Evan: Correct, we need KMS integration and audit logs forwarded to our SIEM, also data residency in EU.
[01:00] Maya: Noted. On the legal side — Lena, can you give us your top three MSA concerns so we can address live?
[01:10] Dr. Lena Ortiz: Sure — indemnity cap sizing, audit rights and subcontractor disclosure. Also retention and breach notification timelines in the DPA look a bit long for us.
[01:22] Maya: Ok, indemnity — we usually accept a mutual cap tied to annual contract value; Ravi — any impact to ops or SLAs if we increase transparency around subcontractors?
[01:32] Ravi: Operationally no, we can disclose major infra partners, truth is we use cloud GPU providers and some edge caching providers. There might be sensitive IP in build pipelines but that's separate.
[01:44] Marcus: On the audit logs — can you stream to S3 or push to our splunk? We prefer push but S3 is ok.
[01:51] Maya: Yes we can do push to your SIEM or S3 with KMS-wrapped keys.
[02:00] Priya: Pricing — can we recap committed vs burst? We need to show finance a predictable monthly burn.
[02:08] Maya: Absolutely. For committed we propose a reserved capacity monthly commit with X GPUs, discounted unit rate. Burst above commit billed at higher rate with automated fallback to cheaper model variants if needed. We'll send a pricing worksheet.
[02:20] Priya: Do you allow metered-only without a commit? Some vendors do, but finance prefers some predictability.
[02:27] Maya: Metered-only is possible for hosted; for dedicated reserved capacity we do monthly commits. We'll include both options in the sheet.
[02:35] Dr. Lena Ortiz: Back to the DPA — breach notification window is 72 hours in your draft but we'd like 48 where feasible. Also we need clarity on data deletion requests and certification evidence for ISO/SOC.
[02:48] Maya: We can accept 48 for priority incidents; for others 72. We will attach SOC2 Type II and ISO27001 certs. I'll include the cert pack link.
[03:00] Evan: KMS — do we support HSM or customer-managed keys across the private deployment?
[03:05] Ravi: Yes, in private we can integrate with your cloud KMS or on-prem HSM for key wrapping. Slight variations depending on region, but EU KMS is supported.
[03:15] Marcus: How about KV cache and model variants — we need to understand latency tradeoffs if you quantize a model.
[03:23] Ravi: Good q — quantization reduces memory and cost but can add small quality regressions; we provide quantization profiles and measured quality deltas. ETA on benchmarks — we'll share our benchmark spreadsheet as part of the pilot pack.
[03:36] Dr. Lena Ortiz: Ok indemnity cap — we prefer a higher cap for IP infringement claims versus general breach. Is that negotiable?
[03:45] Maya: We typically separate IP indemnity carve-outs, yes we can look at language and align on a higher cap for IP. We'll propose specific numbers in the redline.
[03:55] Priya: Timeline — what's realistic for onboarding and pilot? We need procurement sign-off by Jan first week.
[04:02] Maya: If we start the pilot this month and Atlas provides traffic samples, a 2-week pilot is possible; procurement sign-off by early Jan seems feasible.
[04:12] Priya: Ok good, we'll aim for PO submission by Jan 5.
[04:18] Marcus: For the pilot, what's the typical runbook?
[04:22] Ravi: It's usually a 2-hour smoke with sample traffic, then 48-hour stress run if needed. We'll provide the runbook and resource checklist.
[04:32] Maya: I'll put that in next steps.
[04:36] Dr. Lena Ortiz: A couple of specific legal items — data residency clause, deletion certification and subcontractor list. Also the SLA credits formula: currently it's tied to monthly uptime percentage, we want clarity on calculation.
[04:50] Maya: SLA credits are calculated as a percentage of monthly fees, pro rata to downtime beyond the SLO. We'll add examples in the SLA doc; typical SLO is 99.9 for hosted; for dedicated we can target 99.95 depending on configuration.
[05:04] Dr. Lena Ortiz: Is the 99.95 backed by financial credits or simply best-effort?
[05:09] Maya: Dedicated comes with SLA-backed credits, yes. We'll make sure the MSA includes the credit table for each tier.
[05:16] Priya: Any procurement paperwork like W9/Tax forms?
[05:20] Maya: We'll attach vendor onboarding packet including W9, bank remit, and standard PO instructions.
[05:25] Evan: Security question — do you provide KMS key rotation logs and proof of deletion when a contract ends?
[05:32] Ravi: Yes, we can provide key rotation history and a deletion attestation. For on-prem/private deployments we can coordinate your HSM admin for key destruction events.
[05:42] Marcus: Ok, can you confirm data flow? i.e., does any PII or sensitive datasets leave our VPC in private deployment? We need assurance they remain in our control.
[05:53] Maya: In private, no customer data leaves the customer's VPC without your explicit routing. For hosted we offer encryption at rest and transit plus optional KMS. We'll document the exact flows.
[06:05] Dr. Lena Ortiz: On audit rights — we need periodic audits and the right to request SOC2 test results and supplementary reports.
[06:12] Maya: We can provide SOC2 reports and support auditor questionnaires; for on-site audits we'll coordinate but usually provide remote evidence.
[06:20] Priya: Pricing — one more question, are there minimum commitment months? Our finance requires a 12-month commitment for capital planning.
[06:27] Maya: We have flexible terms. Committed reserved capacity usually comes with a 12-month term to get the best rates. We'll detail options.
[06:34] Marcus: For the pilot environment, can we use a subset of Atlas data or synthetic traffic? We want to avoid exposing PHI in the test.
[06:42] Ravi: Yes, synthetic or anonymized traffic works fine, and it's often faster to start. If you need model performance on real de-identified traffic we can do that with a DPA addendum.
[06:53] Dr. Lena Ortiz: DPA addendum — what about subprocessors disclosure cadence? Quarterly is ok for us.
[06:59] Maya: Quarterly disclosure is standard; we also post an up-to-date subprocessor list on our compliance portal.
[07:08] Priya: Ok curious on onboarding time — if we sign PO Jan 5, when can we start production?
[07:14] Maya: Typical timeline: pilot within 1 week of paperwork, production in 2-4 weeks depending on migration complexity. We'll provide a timeline matrix.
[07:24] Marcus: Network-wise — will you require us to open outbound ports or can you peer?
[07:28] Ravi: We support both peering and managed peering; for private deployments peering with VPC is preferred, minimal open ports required. We'll share a network connectivity guide.
[07:38] Dr. Lena Ortiz: A legal nuance — liability period for data breaches; our counsel prefers a 2-year window for claims. Is that compatible?
[07:46] Maya: We can consider a 2-year window for certain claims; we'll flag it for legal review.
[07:52] Priya: Is there a standard discount schedule for multi-year commits?
[07:56] Maya: Yes multi-year gets incremental discounts; we'll include a pricing table for 12 and 24 month terms.
[08:02] Marcus: One more technical — model rollback and version pinning during rollout, we need deterministic behavior for validation. How do you handle that?
[08:10] Ravi: We support model version pinning and can do canary rollouts with automatic rollback rules. We'll show the console flow.
[08:20] Dr. Lena Ortiz: Ok if you could send redlines today that would be helpful.
[08:24] Maya: We will aim to send redlined MSA and DPA by Monday.
[08:28] Priya: Monday would be great.
[08:31] Maya: Final items — onboarding docs, pilot runbook, pricing worksheet, cert pack link and redlines. Anything else?
[08:39] Evan: Please include sample SIEM integration steps.
[08:43] Ravi: Will do.
[08:46] Marcus: We'll assemble traffic profiles and a short statement of success criteria for the pilot.
[08:51] Dr. Lena Ortiz: I'll target legal comments back by Dec 23.
[08:56] Maya: Awesome. Quick recap of next steps — Maya sends MSA/DPA redlines and certs, Ravi shares pilot runbook and benchmarks, Atlas provides traffic profile and legal comments.
[09:07] Priya: Thanks everyone.
[09:10] Maya: Thanks, we'll follow up in email with attachments and schedule the pilot slot.
[09:14] [crosstalk] Speaker 1: Thanks.
[51:30] [call ends]
